name: Algedi
description: A star 32 parsecs away, 8.1 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 100064: radius 8.106 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 38.126 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.05) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 100064: effective temperature 5041 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.037)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 2.9 from 2014ApJ...785...94L; the 15 published values span log g 1.75 to 3.3, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.6% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 100064: distance 32.447 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.006), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 32 parsecs away, 8.1 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 38 times the Sun's luminosity at 5,041 K, so 8.106 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 100064: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Alpha Capricorni
quotes.card: Alpha Capricorni is an optical double star in the constellation of Capricornus.
quotes.introduction: The two physically unrelated components are designated:α1 Capricorni α2 Capricorni.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 6880093650314169984 (quality A), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none
